# Configuration reference

Every zeroauthy setting, generated from the configuration code, so this page
always matches the server. For a worked production file see
[examples/zeroauthy.yaml](../examples/zeroauthy.yaml); for the steps around it
see [deployment](deployment.md).

## How settings are read

- **Sources and precedence.** Built-in defaults, then the YAML file, then
  `ZEROAUTHY_*` environment variables. An environment variable overrides the
  same key in the file.
- **The file** is named by `--config` (`-c`) or by the `ZEROAUTHY_CONFIG` variable.
  Without either, only defaults and environment variables apply.
- **Environment variable names** are `ZEROAUTHY_` plus the key path in upper
  case, with `__` (two underscores) between levels: `storage.dsn` is
  `ZEROAUTHY_STORAGE__DSN`, `security.rate_limit.token.burst` is
  `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__RATE_LIMIT__TOKEN__BURST`. Single underscores are part
  of a key name.
- **Strict keys.** An unknown key in the file, or any unknown variable starting
  with `ZEROAUTHY_` (other than `ZEROAUTHY_CONFIG`), stops the server at startup.
- **Values in environment variables** are text converted to the key's type:
  booleans `true`/`false` (or `1`/`0`), integers and numbers in decimal, and
  durations in Go syntax (`90s`, `5m`, `720h`; there is no `d` unit).
- **Lists.** In YAML write a normal list. An environment variable sets a list
  with exactly one entry; its value is not split on commas or spaces. The
  exception is `server.trusted_proxy_cidrs`, which itself accepts
  comma-separated entries (`ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS=10.0.0.0/8,192.168.0.0/16`).
  For several entries of any other list, use the file.
- **Secrets.** Keys marked **secret** hold credentials; their defaults are never
  shown here. Prefer the `_file` variant where one exists
  (`security.master_key_file`) and keep passwords out of the YAML file, for
  example in `ZEROAUTHY_STORAGE__DSN` or `ZEROAUTHY_EMAIL__SMTP__PASSWORD`.

## Minimal container start

The Docker image already sets `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__LISTEN=:8080`,
`ZEROAUTHY_STORAGE__DSN=sqlite:///data/zeroauthy.db` (SQLite in the `/data`
volume) and `ZEROAUTHY_STORAGE__AUTO_MIGRATE=true`. On top of that you must set:

- `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__SYSTEM_HOST` (the console's host, for example
  `system.localhost:8443`), or `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__BASE_DOMAIN`, which makes it
  default to `system.<base_domain>`.
- `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__MASTER_KEY` (base64 of 32 random bytes:
  `openssl rand -base64 32`) or `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__MASTER_KEY_FILE` (a path to a
  file holding it). It is required with persistent storage; back it up, as the
  database is unreadable without it.

Without `server.tls_cert_file` and `server.tls_key_file` (or `server.acme`) the
server speaks plain HTTP, so put a TLS-terminating proxy in front of it or
mount a certificate. The [quickstart](quickstart.md) shows a full `docker run`.

## Settings

### Top-level keys

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seed` | `ZEROAUTHY_SEED` | string | — | `seed` is an optional path to a declarative seed file applied at startup. |
| `seed_mode` | `ZEROAUTHY_SEED_MODE` | string | `apply` | `seed_mode` is "apply" (the default: the seed overwrites what it defines at every start) or "create_only" (it only creates what is missing, so edits made in the console survive a restart). |

### `server`

`server` configures the listener, host names, proxies and TLS.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server.listen` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__LISTEN` | string | `:8080` | `server.listen` is the address of the HTTP(S) listener, host:port or :port. |
| `server.base_domain` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__BASE_DOMAIN` | string | — | `server.base_domain` makes tenant "acme" reachable at acme.&lt;`server.base_domain`&gt;. |
| `server.system_host` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__SYSTEM_HOST` | string | — | `server.system_host` is the host of the system tenant, which serves the console at /admin. It defaults to system.&lt;`server.base_domain`&gt; and is required when `server.base_domain` is empty. No other tenant may use it. |
| `server.trust_proxy_headers` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS` | bool | `false` | `server.trust_proxy_headers` honors X-Forwarded-Host. Enable it only behind a proxy that sets the header. Deprecated without `server.trusted_proxy_cidrs`. |
| `server.trusted_proxy_cidrs` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` | list of string | — | `server.trusted_proxy_cidrs` lists the immediate peers allowed to act as proxies: self-managed custom-domain proxies, and the only peers whose forwarded headers `server.trust_proxy_headers` honors once any are listed. Entries may also be comma-separated (one environment variable). |
| `server.tls_cert_file` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__TLS_CERT_FILE` | string | — | `server.tls_cert_file` is a PEM certificate chain; with `server.tls_key_file` the listener serves HTTPS. Read at startup. |
| `server.tls_key_file` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__TLS_KEY_FILE` | string | — | `server.tls_key_file` is the PEM private key of `server.tls_cert_file`. Set both or neither. |
| `server.tls_self_signed` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__TLS_SELF_SIGNED` | bool | `false` | `server.tls_self_signed` serves HTTPS with a certificate from a throwaway CA that is generated in memory at every start. It is for test environments (CI, E2E, docker compose), where Auth0 SDKs need an HTTPS issuer, and cannot be combined with tls_cert_file/tls_key_file or `server.acme`. The certificate covers localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, the system host, the base domain and \*.base_domain, tenant domains, and tls_self_signed_hosts; tenant domains added later get a certificate on first connection. |
| `server.tls_self_signed_ca_file` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__TLS_SELF_SIGNED_CA_FILE` | string | — | `server.tls_self_signed_ca_file` receives the throwaway CA certificate (PEM, never its key) at startup so test clients can trust it, for example through NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS or SSL_CERT_FILE. Requires tls_self_signed. |
| `server.tls_self_signed_hosts` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__TLS_SELF_SIGNED_HOSTS` | list of string | — | `server.tls_self_signed_hosts` lists extra DNS names or IP addresses (no port) the self-signed certificate covers, such as a docker compose service name. Entries may also be comma-separated (one environment variable). Requires tls_self_signed. |

#### `server.acme`

`server.acme` is opt-in automatic certificate issuance for managed custom domains and the hosted wildcard. It never disables certificate validation.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server.acme.enabled` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__ACME__ENABLED` | bool | `false` | `server.acme.enabled` turns on ACME certificate issuance. |
| `server.acme.directory_url` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__ACME__DIRECTORY_URL` | string | `https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory` | `server.acme.directory_url` is the CA's ACME directory (HTTPS only); accounts are bound to it, so staging and production never share an account. |
| `server.acme.email` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__ACME__EMAIL` | string | — | `server.acme.email` is the ACME account contact address; required when enabled. |
| `server.acme.terms_accepted` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__ACME__TERMS_ACCEPTED` | bool | `false` | `server.acme.terms_accepted` accepts the CA's terms of service; it must be true when enabled. |
| `server.acme.deployment_id` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__ACME__DEPLOYMENT_ID` | string | — | `server.acme.deployment_id` is a stable identifier shared by every replica; it binds sealed TLS material to this deployment. |
| `server.acme.challenge` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__ACME__CHALLENGE` | string | — | `server.acme.challenge` is http-01 or tls-alpn-01; there is no hidden fallback. |
| `server.acme.http_listen` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__ACME__HTTP_LISTEN` | string | — | `server.acme.http_listen` serves HTTP-01 challenges (default :80); it must be empty for tls-alpn-01. |
| `server.acme.ca_bundle_file` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__ACME__CA_BUNDLE_FILE` | string | — | `server.acme.ca_bundle_file` adds trust roots for the CA's issued chains. |
| `server.acme.workers` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__ACME__WORKERS` | integer | `2` | `server.acme.workers` is the number of concurrent certificate workers in this process, 1 to 8. |

##### `server.acme.hosted_wildcard`

`server.acme.hosted_wildcard` issues base_domain and \*.base_domain through DigitalOcean DNS-01. The token stays in a deployment file, never in tenant state.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server.acme.hosted_wildcard.enabled` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__ACME__HOSTED_WILDCARD__ENABLED` | bool | `false` | `server.acme.hosted_wildcard.enabled` issues the hosted wildcard; it needs server.acme.enabled and server.base_domain. |
| `server.acme.hosted_wildcard.zone` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__ACME__HOSTED_WILDCARD__ZONE` | string | — | `server.acme.hosted_wildcard.zone` is the DigitalOcean DNS zone containing base_domain. |
| `server.acme.hosted_wildcard.token_file` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__ACME__HOSTED_WILDCARD__TOKEN_FILE` | string | — | `server.acme.hosted_wildcard.token_file` is the path of a file holding the DigitalOcean API token; required when enabled. |

#### `server.custom_domains`

`server.custom_domains` is deployment policy for API custom domains.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server.custom_domains.origin_domain` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__CUSTOM_DOMAINS__ORIGIN_DOMAIN` | string | — | `server.custom_domains.origin_domain` is the operator DNS suffix of private origin aliases (cd-&lt;hex&gt;.&lt;origin_domain&gt;); it defaults to base_domain. |
| `server.custom_domains.dns_resolver` | `ZEROAUTHY_SERVER__CUSTOM_DOMAINS__DNS_RESOLVER` | string | — | `server.custom_domains.dns_resolver` (host:port) answers ownership-proof and diagnostic lookups; it defaults to the host's first resolv.conf nameserver. |

### `storage`

`storage` selects the database.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `storage.dsn` | `ZEROAUTHY_STORAGE__DSN` | string, **secret** | — | `storage.dsn` selects the driver: memory://, sqlite://, postgres:// (or postgresql://), mysql://. plugin:// comes with the gRPC plugin host. |
| `storage.auto_migrate` | `ZEROAUTHY_STORAGE__AUTO_MIGRATE` | bool | `false` | `storage.auto_migrate` applies pending schema migrations at startup. When false, serve refuses to start against a schema that is behind or ahead; run zeroauthy migrate first. |

### `security`

`security` holds the master key and server-wide attack protection limits.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `security.master_key` | `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__MASTER_KEY` | string, **secret** | — | `security.master_key` is a base64-encoded 32-byte key. Prefer `security.master_key_file`. |
| `security.master_key_file` | `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__MASTER_KEY_FILE` | string | — | `security.master_key_file` is the path of a file holding the base64 master key. Set only one of `security.master_key` and `security.master_key_file`. |
| `security.login_max_attempts` | `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | integer | `10` | `security.login_max_attempts` failed logins for one account within the lockout window lock that account for `security.login_lockout_seconds`. Per-IP limits are ten times higher. |
| `security.login_lockout_seconds` | `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__LOGIN_LOCKOUT_SECONDS` | integer | `900` | `security.login_lockout_seconds` is how long an account stays locked after `security.login_max_attempts` failures. |
| `security.device_activation_txn_max_misses` | `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__DEVICE_ACTIVATION_TXN_MAX_MISSES` | integer | `5` | Device activation limits wrong user codes. The transaction limit (misses on one device code) must be at least 1. The IP and tenant limits are off at 0. |
| `security.device_activation_ip_max_misses` | `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__DEVICE_ACTIVATION_IP_MAX_MISSES` | integer | `10` | `security.device_activation_ip_max_misses` wrong user codes from one IP lock that IP out of device activation; 0 turns the limit off. |
| `security.device_activation_ip_lockout_seconds` | `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__DEVICE_ACTIVATION_IP_LOCKOUT_SECONDS` | integer | `900` | `security.device_activation_ip_lockout_seconds` is how long the IP lockout lasts. |
| `security.device_activation_tenant_max_misses` | `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__DEVICE_ACTIVATION_TENANT_MAX_MISSES` | integer | `1000` | `security.device_activation_tenant_max_misses` wrong user codes in one tenant within `security.device_activation_tenant_window_seconds` pause its device activation; 0 turns the limit off. |
| `security.device_activation_tenant_window_seconds` | `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__DEVICE_ACTIVATION_TENANT_WINDOW_SECONDS` | integer | `600` | `security.device_activation_tenant_window_seconds` is the window the tenant limit counts misses in. |
| `security.device_activation_tenant_lockout_seconds` | `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__DEVICE_ACTIVATION_TENANT_LOCKOUT_SECONDS` | integer | `60` | `security.device_activation_tenant_lockout_seconds` is how long the tenant pause lasts. |

#### `security.breached_passwords`

`security.breached_passwords` configures the breached password checker used by tenants' breached password detection.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `security.breached_passwords.mode` | `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__BREACHED_PASSWORDS__MODE` | string | `off` | `security.breached_passwords.mode` is off, range (the Pwned Passwords range API over HTTPS, sending only a five-character hash prefix) or file (a local sorted corpus). |
| `security.breached_passwords.file` | `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__BREACHED_PASSWORDS__FILE` | string | — | `security.breached_passwords.file` is the path of the sorted HASH:COUNT SHA-1 corpus; required in file mode. |

#### `security.rate_limit`

`security.rate_limit` is the general Authentication API request limit.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `security.rate_limit.enabled` | `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__RATE_LIMIT__ENABLED` | bool | `true` | `security.rate_limit.enabled` turns the limit on. |
| `security.rate_limit.max_tracked_keys` | `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__RATE_LIMIT__MAX_TRACKED_KEYS` | integer | `50000` | `security.rate_limit.max_tracked_keys` caps the (tenant, IP) buckets of each group; past it the least recently used bucket is dropped. |
| `security.rate_limit.max_concurrent_secret_verifications` | `ZEROAUTHY_SECURITY__RATE_LIMIT__MAX_CONCURRENT_SECRET_VERIFICATIONS` | integer | `0` | `security.rate_limit.max_concurrent_secret_verifications` caps legacy (argon2id) client secret checks running at once in this process; 0 means GOMAXPROCS, at least 4. It applies even when the limit is disabled. |

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email.driver` | `ZEROAUTHY_EMAIL__DRIVER` | string | `log` | log (writes mail to the server log; default), dir or smtp |
| `email.from` | `ZEROAUTHY_EMAIL__FROM` | string | `zeroauthy@localhost` | sender address, optionally "Name &lt;address&gt;"; default "zeroauthy@localhost" |
| `email.dir` | `ZEROAUTHY_EMAIL__DIR` | string | — | directory the dir driver writes messages to; required with it |
| `email.log_links` | `ZEROAUTHY_EMAIL__LOG_LINKS` | bool | `false` | `email.log_links` makes the log driver print reset links in full. Off by default: a logged link lets anyone who reads the log reset a password. |
| `email.allow_local_smtp` | `ZEROAUTHY_EMAIL__ALLOW_LOCAL_SMTP` | list of string | — | `email.allow_local_smtp` permits explicit host:port targets that resolve to private addresses. Leave empty in production unless local relay use is deliberate. |

`events` configures event streams (webhook and EventBridge delivery and server-sent events).

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `events.retention` | `ZEROAUTHY_EVENTS__RETENTION` | duration | `168h` (7 days) | `events.retention` is how long events are kept; at least 24h. |
| `events.max_streams` | `ZEROAUTHY_EVENTS__MAX_STREAMS` | integer | `10` | `events.max_streams` is the event stream quota per tenant. |
| `events.max_connections` | `ZEROAUTHY_EVENTS__MAX_CONNECTIONS` | integer | `4` | `events.max_connections` caps concurrent server-sent event connections per tenant on each server instance. |
| `events.allow_private_networks` | `ZEROAUTHY_EVENTS__ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS` | bool | `false` | `events.allow_private_networks` permits webhook targets on private, loopback and link-local addresses, which are refused by default. |
| `events.allow_insecure_http` | `ZEROAUTHY_EVENTS__ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP` | bool | `false` | `events.allow_insecure_http` permits plain-HTTP webhook targets; for tests and development only. |

### `bootstrap`

`bootstrap` creates the first console operator on an empty install.

| Key | Environment variable | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bootstrap.admin_email` | `ZEROAUTHY_BOOTSTRAP__ADMIN_EMAIL` | string | — | `bootstrap.admin_email`, when set and the system tenant has no operator, makes the server create that operator at start and log a one-time setup link. It never takes a password. |
